title: City Council District 3
statement: What is happening in San Antonio is not a mystery and it is not a mood swing — sentiment there dropped from 0.04 to -0.16 while the city sits at 0.02, and retail vitality fell from 6.43 to 5.22 in the same cycle. That is a neighborhood losing its footing on the commercial blocks while Fruitvale, next door in my own district, is growing. So this week I answer Director Vance's question straight: the OARI briefing and the Fruitvale transit-review notices exist, they were provided, and I will not let a paperwork question become an excuse to skip East Oakland again. I am not opening a new program this week — I am finishing the record I owe, and I am telling San Antonio that when I walk its corridors I am listening for what merchants are actually losing, not waiting for sentiment to turn on its own.

payload.text: Director Vance — the records you are asking for are the district's briefing and transit-review notice records, and here is what I can put on the record plainly. The D3 East Oakland community briefing was scheduled in Fruitvale, in daylight, with the Fruitvale data and response times on the table, and the residents who were promised access were told where and when. On the OARI venue: the briefing was held at a Fruitvale neighborhood venue, not an East Oakland site, and I will say that plainly rather than let the notice read as if the venue were something it was not — that choice was mine, made so the Fruitvale data could be walked through with the people it describes. The transit-review notices went out through the Fruitvale Transit Hub intake channel, and Delia Vargas-Ruiz, the Transit Hub D3 intake liaison, is the named contact for any resident who says they did not receive one. What I am committing to: the venue, the notice dates, and the access provided will be written into a single district record so no resident has to take my word for it, and the Fruitvale review stays open to San Antonio and East Oakland residents on the same terms. If any notice did not land, the intake channel is where I want it reported so it can be fixed rather than argued about.

numberMoved: San Antonio sentiment -0.16 vs city 0.020; crime index 0.73 vs city 0.647; retail vitality 5.22 (from 6.43); D3 approval 59
